business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction; standard SARL seated in metropolitan territory)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codification; unitary system with commercial courts and Cour de cassation appellate review)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49 and 54 - freedom of establishment and right to incorporate a SARL
France - People's Republic of China Double Taxation Convention (signed 30 November 1984, in force 21 December 1985; amended by Protocol of 26 November 2013, in force 1 January 2015)
France - People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 30 May 1984, in force 11 March 1985)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; not yet in force, pending ratification)

Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD/Council of Europe; in force for France 1 September 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and L.562-1 to L.562-15, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Décret n°2018-284 of 18 April 2018 (UBO register rules); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-123 and R.123-224 (beneficial ownership declaration at registration in the Registre National des Entreprises, RNE); INPI UBO declaration form Cerfa n°15618*02 with Arrêté of 2 September 2020; AMF Règlement général Book VI (PEP and sanctions screening for regulated intermediaries); TRACFIN established under Article L.561-21 CMF; sanctions under Articles L.561-45 and L.561-47 CMF (fines up to EUR 375,000 and imprisonment for criminal non-disclosure).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each UBO and proposed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence (e.g., Chinese Notary Office) and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (apostille section)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (China acceded as of 7 November 2023); consular legalization by the French Embassy where apostille is unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or beneficial owner that is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of origin (e.g., Administration for Market Regulation in China or Companies House equivalent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility undertaking or licensed bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth / source of funds declaration letter accompanied by bank reference letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Signed by each UBO and countersigned by the issuing licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of every apostilled exhibit for submission to the French registry and banks
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation under French law; not subject to apostille but must be permanently attached to the notarized original for filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all UBOs, gérants, and authorised signatories against (i) the French national asset-freeze list ('Gels d'avoirs' maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor); (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 as amended); (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the OFAC SDN List for any USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe and PayPal); and (v) PEP databases (World-Check Risk Intelligence or equivalent). Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP match, high-risk third-country nationality, opacity in funding sources, or round-tripping structure. Screening results must be documented and refreshed before incorporation, upon any change of control, and continuously per Articles L.561-6 and L.561-10 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with name availability and prior-rights data via data.inpi.fr (INPI) and infogreffe.fr (Greffes des tribunaux de commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the mandatory official language of all statutory filings (Constitution of 4 October 1958, Article 2; Loi n°94-665 of 4 August 1994, 'Loi Toubon'). The corporate name (dénomination sociale) of a SARL may include foreign terms, but for recognition in the RNE and issuance of the Kbis the name must be expressed in Latin script; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must be non-deceptive, contrary to public policy (ordre public et bonnes mœurs), and distinguishable from existing French and EU-protected designations. All constitutional documents and the Kbis must be in French; any foreign-language clause in the statutes must be accompanied by a sworn French translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit / Mutualité / Assurance / Réassurance - requires prior authorisation of the ACPR
Bourse / Valeurs mobilières / Fonds d'investissement - requires prior authorisation of the AMF
Mairie / Préfecture / Ministère / République / État / Administration / Police / Gendarmerie - misleading reference to French public authority, requires reasoned ministerial consent
Chambre de commerce / Chambre des métiers / Ordre / Fédération / Syndicat / Association - protected representative or professional body designations
Avocat / Notaire / Expert-comptable / Architecte / Médecin / Pharmacien - regulated professional titles reserved for registered professionals
France / Français - sensitive token requiring genuine French character of the undertaking; misleading use actionable under Article L.711-6 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal pre-incorporation name reservation system; priority over the name is secured by filing the complete incorporation dossier. The 30-day window denotes the typical period from submission at the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises to issuance of the Kbis during which registry objections surface. Upon rejection: (i) request a written, reasoned decision from the Greffier; (ii) file a motivated administrative appeal before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce (or the Tribunal Judiciaire in Alsace-Moselle) within one month of notification under Article 52 of Décret n°84-406 of 30 May 1984; (iii) alternatively, re-file immediately with a revised distinctive element (add a prefix, acronym, or secondary word); or (iv) where rejection invokes a prior right, obtain a coexistence or consent letter from the prior rights holder or initiate proceedings to invalidation of the conflicting mark. No extension mechanism exists; a rejected name can only be cured by resubmission or judicial appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible under conditions. Article L.123-11-3 of the Code de commerce and Décret n°86-130 of 28 January 1986 regulate commercial domiciliation. An e-commerce SARL engaged in online retail of automotive replacement parts, having no physical store front, may domicile its registered office at a licensed centre de domiciliation (declared to the Préfecture) provided the centre offers actual physical reception facilities for service of process and official correspondence during business hours. A pure mailbox service without physical reception is non-compliant. The domiciliation contract must be annexed to the articles of association and disclosed to the Greffe; banks and payment providers (Stripe, PayPal) generally accept a licensed domiciliation address for this low-risk activity if a distinct postal address is simultaneously reported.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low to moderate - approximately 15% probability per year of unannounced on-site inspection by the Greffe or the DGFiP tax auditor at the registered office, in line with standard verification of effective management seat. Probability rises to approximately 35% if the SARL is later registered as importer of record or utilises customs bonded storage for imported automotive parts, triggering DGFiP 'contrôle sur pièces et sur place' policy and customs post-clearance audit checks.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting fee - SARL articles of association (statuts), corporate governance annexes, UBO declaration support, and incorporation project management
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Incorporation law firm (Avocat - commercial and corporate practice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: fixed fee EUR 900 - EUR 1,200 excluding VAT; hourly rate EUR 150 - EUR 250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and distinctiveness clearance search - INPI data.inpi.fr database, RNE cross-checks, and EUIPO/domain pre-screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI statutory fees plus legal research disbursements of counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: EUR 50 per trademark class (electronic filing); combined market benchmark for name clearance USD 150 - USD 250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalisation bundle for UBO corporate and personal documents (passports, incumbency certificates, address proofs, bank references)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the document origin country and consular office (e.g., Chinese MFA and French Embassy)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille tariffs approximately USD 10 - USD 40 per document; consular legalisation USD 50 - USD 80 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of all apostilled exhibits by a court-certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 60 - EUR 90 per page for professional legal documents; approximate total of 3 - 4 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation services - 12-month registered office contract with licensed centre de domiciliation (virtual office with physical reception)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed commercial domiciliation company (agréée by the Préfecture)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate: EUR 25 - EUR 35 per month (EUR 300 - EUR 420 per year)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing through the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises including RNE registration, Kbis issuance, and SIREN/SIRET assignment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI (RNE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: approximately EUR 330 - EUR 380 comprised of frais de greffe, droit de greffe, émoluments, and portal processing fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in an approved Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorised legal announcements publisher (éditeur de presse habilité)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated tariff: approximately EUR 155 - EUR 200 based on EUR 0.25 - EUR 0.35 per character

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing and entry into the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee: EUR 24.30 per declaration (Cerfa n°15618*02)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial bank account opening fee and KYC documentation processing at Tier-1 French bank or licensed EMI supporting Stripe/PayPal rails
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank or electronic money institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: USD 100 - USD 250 account opening and due diligence service charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative contingency reserve - courier, certified copies, notarial margin, postage, and miscellaneous disbursements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed contingency reserve of 5-10% of total pre-incorporation budget

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq. governing Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) formation and administration; Civil Code provisions on contracts and civil liability as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; online filing through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (Immatriculation d'une personne morale au RCS) accompanied by the notarised or privately signed Statuts (Articles of Association) and supporting annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital (Article L.223-2). The capital is fixed freely in the Articles of Association. Cash contributions must be deposited on a blocked account opened with a bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts and released only after RCS registration. At least 20% of cash subscriptions must be paid up at incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years. In-kind contributions must be expressly described and approved in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous written resolutions of the shareholder(s) whereby: (1) the Articles of Association are approved and adopted as submitted; (2) the stated share capital is subscribed in full and the cash portion is deposited in a blocked corporate account pursuant to Article L.223-2; (3) the registered office is fixed at the address indicated in Article 4 and the legal representatives are authorised to complete all domiciliation formalities; (4) the person named in Article 8 is appointed sole Manager with authority to manage the company, open bank accounts and represent the company before third parties; and (5) all incorporation filings, legal notice publication and RCS registration steps are expressly authorised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Sign the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private parties / Managing Director; notarisation optional except for in-kind contributions of real property
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French or bilingual form, including the corporate name, registered office address, corporate object (online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories), share capital and contribution schedule, manager designation, and duration. All shareholders must sign the finalised Articles either physically or electronically with an advanced electronic signature.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (Statuts)
Identity documents for each shareholder and appointed manager
French address or domiciliation agreement for the registered office
Statement of no criminal record (extrait de casier judiciaire) or equivalent declaration for the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Articles are returned for non-compliance, amend the deficient clauses and re-sign; any uncertainty in the corporate object must be clarified before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit the Share Capital in a Blocked Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank established in France or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; alternatively a notary acting as depository
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the SARL in formation and deposit the cash subscription amount. Obtain a certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds) stating the amount and identity of the depositing shareholder. The funds remain blocked until the company is registered and the representative is authorised to release them.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Proof of identity of the depositing shareholder and manager
Bank application for corporate account opening
Fund transfer certificate or bank confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit due to documentation gaps, provide the missing shareholder/beneficial owner declarations and re-submit; alternatively select a notary or another bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in an Authorised Journal of Legal Notices (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorised in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice containing the proposed corporate name, SARL legal form, capital amount, registered office address, corporate object, duration, and the manager’s identity. The publisher will issue a certificate granting legal publication (attestation de parution) which is required for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association or draft thereof
Declaration for publication provided by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected or returned, correct the inaccuracies and republish in a compliant JAL; keep the certificate as part of the final filing bundle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Dossier with the RCS via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (online) and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 form online on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, upload the signed Statuts, the capital deposit certificate, the JAL publication attestation, identity documents, the non-criminal record declaration for the manager, and the registered office proof. Pay the filing fee electronically. Submit the dossier; the system generates a receipt which must be kept.
required_dossiers: Form M0 (duly signed)
Signed Statuts
Capital deposit certificate
JAL publication attestation
Identity documents of managers and shareholders
Proof of registered office address (title deed, lease, domiciliation agreement)
Manager's declaration of no criminal record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a request for supplementary information, respond through the Guichet unique portal within the prescribed period, attaching the missing documents. Any formal defect may be cured by amendment filed with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Kbis Extract and Secure Post-Registration Administrative Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; subsequently INSEE, URSSAF, and the competent tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful registration, the Greffe issues the extait Kbis, which is the official criminal record of the company. Automatically or by subsequent application, obtain the SIREN/SIRET numbers, VAT number, and URSSAF registration for employer obligations. Use the Kbis to open final business bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract (issued by the Greffe)
Company seal if required
Bank account details of the company for social contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed or contains incorrect details, file a correction request with the Greffe or by rectification procedure under Article R.123-196 of the Code de commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Undertake Post-Incorporation Labour and Tax Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF; Direction des Finances Publiques; DREETS for labour law inspection units
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL as an employer with URSSAF if hiring staff; file the initial social declarations and set up payroll systems. Confirm VAT registration process (although often automatic via RCS) and provide the Kbis to the tax authorities. Prepare the DUERP (Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels) for workplace safety and post it in the business premises.
required_dossiers: Extait Kbis
Identity documents of staff if any
Fit-up declaration for DREETS if the activity involves specific industrial equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For any irregularity in social or tax enrolment, contact the relevant URSSAF centre or tax office to rectify the registration with a letter explaining the chronology and filing date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) – for occupational and labour safety in warehouse or logistic activities; the Préfecture for any planning or operating authorisation required by local regulations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral industrial operating licence is required for online retail and storage of automotive replacement parts under ISIC 4791. For any warehouse exceeding ICPE thresholds, an operating permit may be required as an Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally Exempt for retail e-commerce of auto parts without combustion or chemical treatment. If the warehouse floor area exceeds 1,000 m² and is used for storage, it may fall under ICPE Rubric 1510 in the 'Déclaration' (registration) regime, requiring a preliminary compliance file but not a full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Where applicable, wastewater must comply with the municipal sewer standards and the French Water Law (R.214-1 et seq.). VOC emissions from packaging adhesives, if used on site, must respect the limits set by the French decree of 14 September 2015 transposing Directive 2004/42/EC. Non-hazardous waste (cardboard, batteries, scrap metal) must be separated and removed by licensed waste collectors; storage of hazardous wastes (e.g. fluids, aerosols) does not exceed the ICPE threshold unless stored above 1 tonne.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local fire service (SDIS) for any premises open to the public (ERP) only if retail showroom is attached. For pure e-commerce logistics premises, compliance with the Labour Code and an attestation of building soundness is required; a Workplace Health and Safety Court inspection may be needed if employees are deployed. A DUERP must be prepared when staff are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate registry: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned SARL: (1) file statutory incorporation documents via the Guichet Unique (single electronic portal), including Articles of Association, proof of registered office (or attestation de domiciliation), and identity documents of the manager(s) and shareholders; (2) obtain SIREN and SIRET numbers automatically from INSEE upon validation of the RCS registration; (3) VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) is allocated automatically by DGFiP to the registered enterprise, with format FR followed by a two-digit key and the 9-digit SIREN; (4) non-EU foreign shareholders must provide a completed Form FR-FTA (Foreign Tax Authority attestation) and may need to appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) subject to DGFiP approval if no permanent establishment exists; (5) the SARL must file an adverse declaration of existence (Formulaire M0 / CERFA 13453) within 30 days of commencement; (6) the entity may request an impôt sur les sociétés (IS) status confirmation from the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) with territorial competence over the registered office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is by default subject to French corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). An irrevocable option for income-tax transparency (régime des sociétés de personnes) is available under Article 239 bis AB of the CGI for SARLs performing commercial, industrial, or artisanal activities with no more than 50 units and meeting specific ownership turnover/profit thresholds. A listed list of eligible enterprises may also elect under the family SARL (SARL de famille) regime. Hybrid mismatch elections under EU ATAD/DAC6 are limited, but taxpayers can file an annual notification and make a choice regarding certain recharacterization rules via the standard tax return. In addition, a SARL can elect to remain subject to IR for the first taxable period provided it meets definitional criteria of a 'small enterprise' (PME under EU Recommendation 2003/361/EC).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 for sales of goods (Article 293 B CGI; franchise en base de TVA) and EUR 36,800 for service providers and liberal activities; e-commerce distance sales exceeding EU-wide EUR 10,000 trigger the OSS (One Stop Shop) registration thresholds, subject to local French registration if intra-EU distance sales exceed the mandatory threshold; an established entity with a fixed establishment in France must register for VAT regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing from phase-in periods starting 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs, requiring issuance of structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) transmitted via a certified Plateforme de Démonétisation (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). Real-time fiscal clearance via the 'Y' scheme is not yet implemented; however, B2C distance sales transactions (including automobile parts) must be reported via the e-reporting module to DGFiP, with the OSS return providing an electronic breakdown. Businesses are required to use API interfaces of the DGFiP 'Partner of Dematerialization' ecosystem; each invoice must receive a unique identification number and a digital fingerprint (empreinte numérique) and be transmitted in near-real-time to the PDP. Failure to implement compliant e-invoicing by statutory deadlines results in penalties up to EUR 15,000 per infraction (later increased to EUR 60,000 for recurring breaches).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (1) sales of goods physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union by the vendor or a third party on its behalf, provided that the goods leave France within 90 days of the invoice date (Customs Code Article 292, CGI Article 291-I); (2) exports placed under an external community transit or export customs procedure; (3) certain services directly linked to exported goods (e.g., freight, inspection, loading) supplied to a non-EU customer are eligible for 0% when ancillary to an effective export. The supplier must obtain and preserve within 1 month (extended to 6 months for retroactive zero-rating claims) a tangible set of transport or customs documents demonstrating physical exit from EU territory; there is no statutory de minimis threshold for letters of weight or postal dispatches, but the French tax administration applies a EUR 850 value cap for light consignments qualifying by declaration only.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Export / DAU - Document Administratif Unique) via the SYDONIX or DELTA/XML clearance system containing the goods description and exit certificate (Exemplaire n°3) stamped by French customs
Bill of Lading (or other transport document: CMR, airway waybill, or postal acceptance receipt) evidencing dispatch from France and arrival in the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / IRC issued by the bank demonstrating the transfer and receipt of foreign exchange proceeds from the non-EU customer within 180 days of shipment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP applies an automatic and reinforced anti-abuse scrutiny to export zero-rating claims; the tax inspector may require immediate proof of the physical exit of goods and may retroactively assess VAT (20%) on all operations not justified within 6 months. Penalties apply: (i) standard late payment interest (intérêts de retard) at 0.20% per month from the due date; (ii) a 40% penalty for wilful inaccuracy (manquement délibéré) under Article 1729 CGI, increased to 80% for fraudulent behavior (abus de droit or manoeuvres frauduleuses) and up to 80% for trafficking in false customs declarations under Customs Code Article 414; (iii) criminal prosecution (Customs offenses) may lead to a fine equal to the amount evaded and confiscation of goods and vehicles. The refund claim can be clawed back with a minimum 10% shall-miss vigilance rule triggering a fiscal prosecutor referral. Intentional falsification of an export document (including backdating of signed proof of arrival) constitutes tax fraud and may be sanctioned with 3 years' imprisonment, EUR 45,000 fine, and disqualification from management functions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), in conjunction with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury), which administers exchange-control policy under the French Code monétaire et financier, in particular Articles L151-1 et seq. and R151-1 et seq.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the French Monetary and Financial Code, no prior exchange-control authorization is required for current-account payments, capital transfers, dividends, royalties, or ordinary profit remittances between France and EU/EEA jurisdictions. Transactions with non-EEA counterparties are also freely executable through licensed banks, subject to AML/KYC, sanctions screening, and balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the Banque de France. Profit remittance is not blocked by exchange controls. A French SARL may distribute dividends to non-resident shareholders through normal banking channels, provided the company complies with French tax withholding rules, applies any applicable tax-treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary protection, and the paying bank receives the usual corporate and tax documentation. The main practical hurdles are therefore tax documentation, VAT/accounting traceability, and AML source-of-funds evidence, not currency convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no general mandatory surrender or forced-conversion requirement on export receipts. There is no statutory conversion ratio and no fixed statutory deadline within which export proceeds must be repatriated or converted into euro. Export invoices may be denominated and collected in freely convertible foreign currency, and proceeds may be retained in euro or foreign-currency accounts domestically or abroad, subject to annual French foreign-account reporting and Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting. The SARL must preserve the underlying documentary chain for each export settlement, including commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents, customs declarations, and bank MT103 confirmations. Intra-EU dispatches must be reported through the Intrastat/Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens scheme when thresholds are met; non-EU exports require export customs declarations. Cash or cash-equivalent transfers of EUR 10,000 or more across the French border are subject to customs declaration, and all wire transfers are monitored by the licensed banking intermediary under French AML rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR account and cross-border FX/clearing account
Capital escrow account and trade finance account
Operational collection account and export settlement rail
Operational account with e-commerce acquiring and daily sweeping
Marketplace settlement account and disbursement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a supplementary collection and payout rail, but not as the primary treasury bank. EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) may passport into France under PSD2 and may hold client funds as safeguarded e-money; however, such funds are not bank deposits and are not protected by the French deposit guarantee fund (FGDR). Offshore/non-EEA digital EMIs without an EU license or a licensed French/EU agent cannot lawfully provide payment services to French residents. For an auto-parts e-commerce treasury, an EEA EMI such as Qonto, Wise Business, or Payoneer may be used for low-value global payouts, multi-currency virtual accounts, and fast settlement from card platform providers, but all statutory capital, tax clearing, LC, and major FX transactions should remain with a Tier-1 licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not mandate that every director physically appear in person, but the bank must comply with mandatory AML/CFT customer due diligence, including identification of all beneficial owners under Articles L561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. In practice, Tier-1 banks will require a physical or secure video-identified interview with at least one managing director (gérant) and full production of the beneficial-owner register (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) filed with the RCS. Remote account opening is feasible only when identity verification meets the bank's electronic-identification standard and the corporate package is complete, including an up-to-date Kbis extract, certified company deeds, apostilled and translated documents for non-French shareholders, tax residence certificates, and source-of-funds evidence. Non-resident directors may, at the bank's discretion, be required to execute a notarized power of attorney in favour of a local French contact or be subjected to enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce in automotive replacement parts with low average ticket and rapid inventory turnover, raising trade-based money-laundering and layering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract not older than three months, certified statutes of the SARL, identity documents of all directors and beneficial owners, UBO register receipt, live e-commerce website and marketplace listings, ERP sales-order ledger, Stripe/PayPal settlement statements, payment-acquirer KYC confirmation, customs and Intrastat/DEB reports, commercial invoices, supplier contracts and purchase orders, stock movement reconciliations, and audited accounting demonstration of gross margins and inventory traceability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or multi-jurisdiction shareholder and beneficial-ownership structure, particularly with shareholders outside the EU/EEA or in jurisdictions subject to enhanced monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date RCS extract including the beneficial-owner declaration, passports and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners, corporate organisation chart, shareholder register, tax residence certificates, bank and wealth-manager references, source-of-funds evidence from qualifying bank statements and asset sale documents, negative sanctions and adverse-media screening, and legal opinion or coordinating counsel letter explaining the legitimate commercial purpose of the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between goods descriptions and payment amounts, advance payments from third-party buyers, or routing of payments by payment aggregators to non-EU beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts and purchase orders, order-level invoices, proof of delivery such as CMR waybills, air waybills, bills of lading, CN 23 customs forms, EU ENS or non-EU export declarations, SWIFT MT103 messages showing beneficiary and remittance fields, product-level classification and compatibility documentation under ISIC 4791, buyer KYC records for B2B clients, and a written treasury memorandum explaining split settlements and aggregator payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback rates, refund disputes, and card-not-present risk on marketplace sales, which can trigger acquirer liability and AML monitoring at the banking and clearing level.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS attestation of compliance, 3-D Secure and authentication logs, refund and dispute handling policy, delivery confirmation data, tracking numbers, customer complaint records, product-quality and warranty documentation, acquirer monthly statements, chargeback history and provisioning analysis, and forecast showing that refund provisions are held in the SARL's operational treasury account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder current-account funds must arrive by bank wire via SEPA or SWIFT MT103, with the remittance narrative stating the legal basis, for example 'SOUSCRIPTION ET LIBÉRATION DU CAPITAL SOCIAL' (subscription and payment of share capital) or 'APPORT EN COMPTE COURANT D'ASSOCIÉ' (shareholder current-account contribution). For non-EU originators, the MT103 should include full field 50F sender details, field 59A beneficiary details, and field 70 purpose narrative containing 'PURP/INTC EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or a similarly explicit purpose reference. The receiving French bank will verify the Kbis extract, shareholder register, capital contribution resolution, and may apply source-of-wealth checks. Funds are free from exchange-control approval, but the bank reports the inward transfer to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics where thresholds apply, and the SARL must evidence the contribution in its statutory accounts and tax filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EU suppliers, settlement is routed via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) using ISO 20022 pain.001. For non-EU suppliers, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for commercial payment, or MT202 COV for bank-to-bank settlement when the underlying payment has already been covered by a separate instruction. For high-value purchases and documentary trade, the SARL may use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued through its Tier-1 bank by SWIFT MT700, with confirmation through a correspondent bank in the supplier's jurisdiction; documentary collections under ICC URC 522 are also permissible. E-commerce card receipts from Stripe and PayPal are settled via card network clearing into the SARL's collection account, with periodic sweeps into the main euro operational account. All payouts must be reconciled to customs entries, import VAT/fiscal records, commercial invoices, and the ERP treasury ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contract with a licensed French or EU credit institution for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY, and other freely convertible commercial currencies

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies without full deliverable settlement in France, provided the underlying cross-border trade exposure is documented and the transaction is executed under a bank ISDA/CSA arrangement
Plain-vanilla FX swap (swap de change) for temporary cross-currency liquidity conversion
Cross-currency swap or cross-currency interest-rate swap aligned with the SARL's actual import receivables and export payables
Purchased long-dated FX options for downside protection, where writing uncovered options is avoided and additional bank suitability documentation is required

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and financial-statement declaration (liasse fiscale no. 2065-SD, with supporting schedules) submitted to the tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) at the registered office's tax district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies, the second working day after 3 May of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal years, within three months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of assessed corporate income tax (increased to 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days after formal notice), monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%, and an additional 5% penalty for late tax payment; persistent defaults may trigger enforced recovery against the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, notes) and related management reports at the Trade and Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within six months after fiscal year-end; deposit within one month after approval; thus normally no later than seven months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year company by 31 July, unless a court extension is obtained)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On failure to deposit, any interested person may obtain a court injunction to deposit; the public prosecutor may demand RCS strike-off (radiation); managing partners may incur personal liability to third parties for resulting damage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration de confirmation des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS, filed with or attached to the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit; any change in shareholding or control additionally requires an updated beneficial-owner declaration within 60 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or stale beneficial-owner data may expose the legal representative to administrative fines and anti-money-laundering penalties; false declarations can lead to criminal sanctions (imprisonment and fine) and may prevent the company from using the RCS registration as effective proof of existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting approving the annual accounts and, where required, discharging the manager
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's statutory minute book and shareholders' attendance records (not transmitted to a public authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each fiscal year-end, unless a shorter period is set in the articles; failure to hold the meeting starts the late-deposit chain for the RCS filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct State fine, but the delay or omission prevents compliance with the one-month deposit deadline, exposes the manager to a court-appointed convocation, and supports the same strike-off and personal-liability risks as the registry deposit item.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three commercial-code thresholds at fiscal year-end: balance-sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Appointments may also be required for subsidiaries/controlling entities or on application by shareholders holding at least one-third of the capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) in accordance with Book I, Title II, Chapter III of the Commercial Code; EU-adopted IFRS governs consolidated accounts of listed companies and may be used for non-listed consolidated accounts where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the RCS, the SARL maintains a current beneficial-owner declaration. The annual confirmation is made at the time of the annual accounts filing: the manager re-certifies that previously filed beneficial-owner data are still exact or files an amended declaration. In the meantime, every transfer of shares or change in control over the company (whether direct or indirect) that alters beneficial ownership must be reflected in the register of members and in an updated RCS beneficial-owner declaration within 60 days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers' decisions and appointments
Minute Book of shareholders' meetings and written resolutions
Share transfer register (registre des mouvements de titres)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $140 – $590 per year for commercial registered-office/domiciliation services including mail handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,300 – $19,500 per year for a small or mid-size retail SARL when an audit is mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and share capital at least 75% held by individuals); Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying research expenditure; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenses; French taxing jurisdiction is unitary at national level with no additional sub-federal corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward (no statutory expiry), but annual absorption is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000; carryback allowed for 1 year up to EUR 1,000,000 (Art. 209 CGI).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultats n° 2065 (liasse fiscale, 2065-SD and 2050 series) filed electronically via EDI-TDFC on impots.gouv.fr; mandatory for all SARLs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly CIT advance payments on Form 2571 due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year filers: file by the second business day after 1 May; non-calendar fiscal years: file within 3 months after the closing date, extended to the next business day if the deadline falls on a weekend or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, APE/NAF code, legal form (SARL), registered office, competent tax office (SIE), fiscal year opening and closing dates, legal representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French Kbis registration data; non-resident legal representatives must appoint an accredited French tax representative and file the mandate annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit or loss transferred from the statutory profit-and-loss account after French GAAP adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recompute revenue and expenses on an accrual basis; convert foreign-currency transactions at the official Banque de France exchange rate used in the statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible add-backs: fines, taxes, penalties, excessive directors' remuneration, non-professional car amortisation, excessive interest charges, non-deductible provisions and gifts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess related-party payments to foreign shareholders; if no arm's-length support exists, the payment must be re-integrated into taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax deductions: depreciation charges, government subsidies, research/innovation tax credits, prior losses applied, intercompany royalties or fees already at arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign IP royalties are deductible only if the beneficial owner has real economic substance and the payment does not fall within the anti-hybrid or abuse-of-law rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result before and after offset of prior-year losses; calculation of the carryforward absorption under the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% annual cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only lawful French-source taxable operations of the e-commerce SARL should be included; no automatic territorial exemption applies to the SARL's foreign sales in the absence of a permanent establishment abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax: 15% tranche on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, 25% on the remaining taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL's CIT liability is computed at entity level regardless of the residence of shareholders; non-resident ownership has no effect on the French headline rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annex tables for depreciation, provisions, capital gains, tax credits, foreign branches, intercompany flow recap and related-party tables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL pays royalties, management fees or interest to a non-resident related party, complete the intercompany annexes and retain contemporaneous TP documentation to support the deduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% statutory increase on assessed CIT; failure to file within 30 days of formal notice: 40% penalty; deliberate misstatement or abuse of law: 80% penalty; late-payment interest of 0.2% per month on unpaid CIT from the first day following the due date; fixed penalty of EUR 100 per omitted annex table; in persistent non-compliance, the tax administration may attach bank accounts and register a tax lien on business assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-resident corporate shareholders under Art. 119 bis-2 CGI; 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate parents holding at least 10% of the SARL's capital for at least 2 years (Parent-Subsidiary Directive); treaty relief commonly reduces the rate to 5% (qualified holding) or 15% (portfolio). Non-resident individuals generally retain a residual 30% levy (12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies) unless an applicable double tax treaty exempts social levies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority, (2) file the certificate together with proof of shareholding and 2-year holding period if alleging EU directive exemption, (3) submit a claim before the paying agent for reduced withholding at source, or alternatively file a refund request with the Direction des Vérifications Nationales et Internationales (DVNI) before 31 December of the second year following the distribution, (4) demonstrate beneficial ownership and absence of an artificial conduit arrangement in line with French GAAR (Art. 205 A CGI).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for patents, trademarks, know-how and copyright paid to non-residents: domestic withholding rate 33⅓% under Art. 182 CGI, with DTA reductions commonly 0-10% and often 0% for software/digital royalties. Interest paid on arm's-length commercial debt to non-resident creditors: no general French withholding tax; however, late-paid or shareholding-linked participating interest may be recharacterised as dividends and subject to 25% withholding. Treaty rates on interest are usually 0% or 5% depending on the DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 of French entity annual net turnover where the SARL belongs to a group whose consolidated turnover or balance-sheet assets exceed EUR 400,000,000 (Art. L.13 AA LPF). Below these thresholds, contemporaneous arm's-length evidence is still required for any cross-border related-party payment; a Master File/Local File becomes compulsory only above those thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but genuine substance is enforced through the general anti-abuse rules: abuse of law (Art. L64 LPF), anti-hybrid and CFC rules (Art. 205 A and 209 B CGI), thin-capitalisation limits (interest deduction restricted to 30% of EBITDA), and the beneficial-ownership test of DTAs. For the e-commerce SARL, substance is evidenced by local employees, physical warehouse or fulfilment premises in France, actual order-processing and after-sales functions, and commercial decisions taken on French territory; failure to demonstrate such substance will trigger disallowance of intercompany deductions, recharacterisation of flows and 80% penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of taxable e-commerce turnover, including unreported Stripe/PayPal settlements, false or backdated invoicing, omission of VAT and CIT, or participation in an organised tax-evasion scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years (Art. 1741 CGI); additional 40% or 80% tax penalty on assessments, monthly 0.2% late-payment interest, publication of the conviction, judicial confiscation of assets and bank account freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL manager is jointly and severally liable for the tax debts and penalties when personally involved in the fraud (Art. 1742 CGI); bankruptcy disqualification, professional ban, travel ban and criminal confiscation may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining the French SARL with no local economic substance, operating as a booking centre for foreign marketplace transactions, artificially shifting profits through inflated management fees, royalties or distribution margins to related entities in low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse-of-law procedure (Art. L64 LPF) leading to a 80% penalty on the under-declared tax, full recharacterisation of the scheme, disallowance of deducted payments, and nullification of claimed treaty benefits; anti-conduit measures under EU GAAR can also deny treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally sued for restitution and contribution to corporate tax deficiencies under 'faute de gestion' actions, and can be held jointly and severally liable when the sham structure was knowingly implemented; commercial courts may impose personal bankruptcy orders and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file and maintain the beneficial ownership register (RBE), failure to identify the real economic owners of the SARL, ignoring suspicious Stripe/PayPal transactions, or refusing to provide information to TRACFIN on request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 30,000 for natural persons and EUR 150,000 for legal entities under the Code monétaire et financier; aggravated money-laundering penalties up to 7 years' imprisonment and EUR 1,000,000 fine where e-commerce flows are concealed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL manager and directors are personally liable for AML control failures; legal entity fines are converted into personal criminal liability when the manager personally directed the omission, with asset confiscation and travel bans on progress.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding a Stripe settlement account, PayPal balance account or foreign bank account with a non-French financial institution (for example PayPal Luxembourg/UK or a US-based merchant account) without declaring it on Form 3916, or understating the aggregated foreign balance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EUR 1,500 penalty per undeclared foreign account, raised to EUR 10,000 where the account's total balance exceeds EUR 10,000; where concealment is used to evade CIT or VAT, criminal sanctions apply under Art. 1741 CGI with up to 3 years' imprisonment and EUR 150,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally control and fail to declare such accounts face personal criminal liability; the corporate veil is pierced by reason of the intentional non-disclosure, allowing attachment of personal assets and a travel ban until the fiscal debt is settled.
